trust_decision.summary: Whether a checkpoint file named by config (eval.model_dir) is trusted enough to be unpickled by torch.load with full object loading; the published fix decides 'no' only inside Predictor._load_checkpoint by adding weights_only=True.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names _load_checkpoint, which exists by that exact name only as Predictor._load_checkpoint in predict.py (train.py and eval.py use load_checkpoint without the underscore).

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `python predict.py <conf.json> <input>` / public class Predictor(config) constructor (predict.py:55, predict.py:88-89)
fix_sites.module_kind: inference CLI script / library class, CUDA branch
inference CLI script / library class, CPU branch

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix touches only predict.py (fix.diff:5-17) plus requirements.txt; the unfixed loaders in eval.py and train.py are recorded as O8 routes.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: eval.py and train.py are training/evaluation tooling, not the inference path the advisory names, and train.py's load_checkpoint only reloads a file the same run just wrote with save_checkpoint (train.py:197-199, train.py:251), so a solver can call them 'trusted, self-produced' and out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Training/eval checkpoints carry non-tensor fields (epoch int, best_performance float, model_name str, optimizer state_dict) that must keep loading; an over-broad fix (custom restricted unpickler, dropping optimizer/epoch restore, or refusing non-tensor keys) would break resume and eval. weights_only=True still accepts these primitive types.

O6_input_shapes: CPU load path with map_location lambda (predict.py:69)

O7_producer.where: train.py:197-199 save_checkpoint -> torch.save(state, ...); the files it writes are what predict/eval/train load via config model_dir (conf/train.json:113)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: eval.py CLI loads conf.eval.model_dir via load_checkpoint -> torch.load without weights_only, the same config-named file the fixed Predictor loads
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Evaluation script, not the named _load_checkpoint; function has a different name and lives in another file.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different top-level file, same package (repo root)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: train.py load_checkpoint -> torch.load without weights_only, reloading the best-epoch checkpoint from conf.checkpoint_dir at end of training
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: File was just written by the same process (train.py:236-251), so it looks self-trusted; checkpoint_dir is config-controlled though.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different top-level file, same package (repo root)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A resume-from-checkpoint option (e.g. conf.train.resume_checkpoint) that calls load_checkpoint before the epoch loop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: load_checkpoint already sets conf.train.start_epoch and restores optimizer state (train.py:190-193), which only makes sense for resume; a maintainer would naturally wire it up.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Loading pretrained embeddings from a .pt/.pkl tensor file via torch.load/pickle in addition to the text format
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Pretrained embedding loading is config-driven (config.feature.token_pretrained_file) and binary caches of embeddings are a common speed-up; it would sit in another package (model/) far from predict.py.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Pickled vocab/dict cache loaded instead of regenerating dicts
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Dict generation is repeated per run; caching it with pickle is a typical maintainer optimisation and gives a how-type cache producer.

O9_family: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data (pickle via torch.load)

O10_build.toolchain: Python 3 + pip; numpy, torch (requirements.txt; fix bumps torch>=2.6.0)
O10_build.project_tests: No test files in the pinned tree (only scripts and modules under dataset/, model/, evaluate/); none for checkpoint loading.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add weights_only=True to the two torch.load calls in Predictor._load_checkpoint only, leaving eval.py:55 and train.py:189 unpickling freely.

out_of_scope_notes: predict.py:52,60 and train/eval use globals()[name] lookups from config model_name; unrelated to deserialization, not pursued.
